nativeFact: Awaiting this async function produces the exact value 'ready'.
notes: Smoke test for the same-fixture native/interpreter pipeline.

nativeFact: Awaiting the controlled async wrapper suspends the caller until its gate opens, allowing a ready MainActor controller to make progress before the wrapper returns.
notes: The controller cannot run inline with Task construction. The host wrapper records entry and yields behind an explicit gate; only the barrier-forced trace is asserted.

nativeFact: A newly created MainActor task does not run inline with its constructor; both tasks complete after the creator reaches a suspension point.
notes: The relative order of 'first' and 'second' is deliberately not asserted.

nativeFact: One hundred sibling MainActor tasks retain the lexical nested type and local index belonging to their own invocation across a forced yield; only completion order is unspecified.
notes: Native support and the interpreter harness both provide parityYield(_:) as an identity gateway with one real Task.yield suspension.

nativeFact: Cancelling a task only after it has entered a cancellable suspension completes it with CancellationError, while an interleaved sibling retains its extension's lexical nested type and completes with 'beta'.
notes: The started barrier forces cancellation-during-suspension. No task-start or sibling-completion order is asserted.

nativeFact: Task.detached does not inherit a TaskLocal value, but an explicitly captured value can be rebound around an async callback and remains visible inside that callback.
notes: The interpreter twin uses a real native detached task and verifies that TaskBoundEvalContext rebinds the exact originating EvaluationTaskContext ID.

nativeFact: One hundred extension-declared async initializers retain their own argument and extension lexical nested type across suspension; sibling completion order is unspecified.
notes: The fixture alternates two nominal types so active initializer and lexical owner state cannot be shared accidentally.

nativeFact: Async initializers preserve success, thrown-error through try?, failable success, and failable nil outcomes across suspension.
notes: Every branch crosses the same real parityYield suspension before deciding its outcome.

nativeFact: Reading await task.value suspends the caller until the task completes and then returns its successful value.
notes: The child is held behind an explicit gate. The opener is created immediately before the value read and cannot run inline on MainActor, so the value read is the suspension that lets it run.

nativeFact: A throwing task preserves its failure across suspension and try await task.value throws it to the awaiting caller.
notes: The operation crosses parityYield before throwing a source enum; the probe asserts catchability, not version-specific error text.

nativeFact: Multiple tasks may await the same task value concurrently and every waiter receives the one completed success value.
notes: Both waiter tasks mark their arrival and then suspend on MainActor before a controller opens the child gate. Relative waiter resume order is unspecified.

nativeFact: Cancelling a task while it awaits another unstructured task's value does not end the value wait or cancel the target; the waiter receives the value and remains marked cancelled.
notes: MainActor isolation guarantees the waiter has entered target.value before the controller can cancel it. The target remains behind a separate gate until after cancellation. Exact output is target-active,waiter-cancelled,handle-cancelled on Swift 6.3.3.

nativeFact: An unstructured task cancelled before it can start still enters its operation, observes cancellation, may return a normal value, and remains marked cancelled.
notes: MainActor isolation prevents the inherited task from starting before the creator cancels it and suspends on value. Exact output is body-ran,body-cancelled,handle-cancelled on Swift 6.3.3.

nativeFact: Reading await task.result suspends until completion and returns success or failure as a Result value without throwing the task failure; get() rethrows the stored failure.
notes: The success is held behind an explicit gate; the failure crosses parityYield, is first inspected by case without try or catch, and is then observed through get().

nativeFact: After a task completes, repeated value and result reads reproduce its stored success or failure; Result.get() continues to rethrow the stored failure.
notes: The first value/result read establishes completion and all later reads target the completed handle. Exact output is value,value,success:value,failure,failure,get-caught on Swift 6.3.3.

nativeFact: A throwing task cancelled after entering a cancellable suspension completes await task.result as a failure Result instead of throwing from the property read.
notes: An explicit started barrier distinguishes cancellation during suspension from cancellation before task start; this fixture asserts only the failure case shape, not error text.

nativeFact: A Task.detached operation may suspend and its handle value awaits completion and returns the operation result.
notes: This first detached-source fixture proves construction, suspension, and value flow. Task-local and executor inheritance require separate probes; priority is covered independently.

nativeFact: An explicit utility priority is visible in its task and inherited by an unstructured Task created inside it; a detached task without an explicit priority starts at medium priority.
notes: No handle is awaited by higher-priority code before the three raw values are captured, so priority escalation cannot contaminate the inheritance observation. Exact output is 17,17,21 on the active Swift 6.3.3 toolchain.

nativeFact: A running background-priority task is escalated to high priority when a high-priority task awaits its value, and a subsequently created unstructured child inherits that effective priority.
notes: The low task records 9 before the high waiter exists. On MainActor, the high task opens the low gate and immediately awaits the low handle with no intervening suspension, so the second read and child creation occur only after waiter registration. Exact output is 9,25,25 on Swift 6.3.3.

nativeFact: High-priority donation propagates through a chain when the awaited task is itself awaiting another task.
notes: MainActor barriers ensure the utility middle task is already awaiting the background bottom task before the high task opens the bottom gate and immediately awaits the middle task. Exact output is 9,25,25 on Swift 6.3.3.

nativeFact: Distinct source @TaskLocal declarations with the same member name retain separate identities; projected withValue is dynamically scoped across suspension, inherited by Task, absent from Task.detached, and restored afterward.
notes: Every task is awaited, so the exact assertion depends only on task-local scope rather than scheduling order. The two defaults and bindings make textual-name aliasing observable, and both synchronous and suspending withValue overloads are exercised. Exact output is primary-default|secondary-default;primary-bound|secondary-default;primary-bound|secondary-sync;primary-bound|secondary-default;primary-default|secondary-default;primary-bound|secondary-bound;primary-bound|secondary-default;primary-default|secondary-default on Swift 6.3.3.

nativeFact: A scoped task-local binding is inherited by an unstructured Task, not inherited by Task.detached, and restored after a nested binding exits.
notes: The same parityWithTaskLocalValue/parityReadTaskLocal declarations are supplied by native and interpreter support. The nested binding crosses a real parityYield suspension. Exact output is parent,parent:child:parent,default.

nativeFact: A task-local scoped binding is removed when its operation throws or is cancelled, so a catch outside the scope observes the inherited parent value.
notes: Both paths use the same source fixture and task-local support declarations. The throwing scope crosses parityYield; the cancellation path uses an explicit wait-started barrier before cancel(). Exact output is parent,parent.

nativeFact: An optional @TaskLocal static variable may omit its initializer; its implicit default is nil and scoped bindings restore that nil value.
notes: The same source declaration and withValue scope run on both sides and cross parityYield. Exact output is nil,bound,nil.

nativeFact: An unstructured Task created by a function may continue after that function returns; it is not a structured child joined at lexical scope exit.
notes: The child waits behind a gate, the creator records returned and exits, and a separate controller opens the gate. The interpreter parity runner uses its explicit drainOwnedTasks host policy.

nativeFact: Discarding the last source-level handle to an unstructured task neither cancels the task nor ends its operation; the task remains alive independently until completion.
notes: The Task result is assigned directly to _, so no source handle survives creation. MainActor gates prove that the task starts, remains active after the drop, and finishes only after explicit release. Exact output is completed,active on Swift 6.3.3.

nativeFact: Cancellation is a cooperative request: a task may catch CancellationError from a cancellable suspension and complete successfully while its handle remains marked cancelled.
notes: The explicit started barrier forces cancellation during suspension. The exact result is success:caught,cancelled; cancellation request state and terminal outcome are asserted separately.

nativeFact: Cancelling an unstructured task does not propagate cancellation to another unstructured Task created inside it.
notes: The parent reaches a cancellable suspension only after storing the child handle. The child remains behind a separate gate until after parent cancellation; exact output is cancelled,child.

nativeFact: Task.sleep suspends without blocking MainActor, and cancelling the sleeping task resumes it by throwing CancellationError.
notes: A separate async helper waits for the explicit started marker before cancellation. The 30-second deadline cannot expire within the five-second process bound; exact output is started,cancelled.

nativeFact: A MainActor task can repeatedly yield its executor until a ready sibling task makes observable progress.
notes: Task creation cannot run the worker inline, so progress requires a suspension. This completion-only liveness probe asserts neither a yield count nor relative scheduler order; every bounded native run returns completed.

nativeFact: An active task cancellation handler runs before cancel() returns, runs only once when cancellation is requested repeatedly, and executes in the cancelling task's dynamic context.
notes: MainActor serialization keeps the operation from resuming until the controller has observed both cancel calls. The uncancelled controller makes Task.isCancelled false inside onCancel; exact output is 0,1,1,false,true,done on Swift 6.3.3. No ready-task scheduler order is asserted.

nativeFact: Registering a cancellation handler in an already-cancelled task invokes it immediately and before the operation begins.
notes: MainActor prevents the task from starting before two cancellation requests. Registration then occurs on that cancelled task, so Task.isCancelled is true in both onCancel and operation; exact output is 1,true,true,operation-cancelled on Swift 6.3.3.

nativeFact: Two nested active cancellation handlers run once in inner-to-outer order before the cancelled operation resumes.
notes: A MainActor started barrier makes both registrations active before cancellation and keeps the worker from resuming during cancel(). Exact output is inner,outer,operation on Swift 6.3.3; no ordering between independent ready tasks is asserted.

nativeFact: A cancellation handler is no longer active after its operation returns or throws, so later cancellation does not invoke it.
notes: MainActor exit barriers place each cancel() strictly after the corresponding handler scope unwinds. Exact output is normal-operation,normal-exit,normal-cancelled,throwing-operation,throwing-exit,throwing-cancelled on Swift 6.3.3; handler event names are deliberately absent.

nativeFact: An async-let initializer starts as a structured child before the parent reads the binding, and awaiting that binding suspends until the child produces its value.
notes: The child marks entry and waits behind an explicit gate. The parent cannot open that gate until the child has started, and it reads the binding only after opening it. Exact output is child-start,parent-open,child-end,value; no unconstrained ready-task order is asserted.

nativeFact: A tuple-pattern async let creates one initializer child whose stored tuple outcome supplies each awaited element binding.
notes: The single initializer waits behind an explicit gate and returns (left, right). Exact output is child-start,parent-open,child-end,left,right in 20 Swift 6.3.3 runs; no unconstrained ready-task order is asserted.

nativeFact: Every initializer in one multi-binding async-let declaration starts as a distinct child before either binding is read; each awaited name receives its own child result.
notes: Both children increment a MainActor start count before waiting on one shared gate, so parent-open cannot occur until both are active. Swift 6.3.3 happened to produce one total order in 20 runs, but only the barrier, result-dependency, and parent program-order edges are asserted.

nativeFact: Separate async-let declarations unwind in reverse registration order: the later child's cancellation and join complete before teardown of the earlier child begins.
notes: Both children enter 30-second cancellable suspensions before scope-exit. Swift 6.3.3 produced one total trace in 20 runs, but the fixture asserts only entry before exit, later-declaration cleanup before earlier-declaration cleanup, and full cleanup before after-scope.

nativeFact: Cancelling an owner propagates the request to its unread async-let child; after source catches cancellation, leaving the owner scope still joins that child before the parent task value completes.
notes: The child and parent are both inside 30-second cancellable suspensions before cancel-issued. Across 100 Swift 6.3.3 runs, child and parent cancellation observation had two relative orders, so only propagation, per-task program order, and the final structured join are asserted.

nativeFact: Leaving a lexical scope without reading an async-let binding cancels the child and waits for that child to finish before execution continues after the scope.
notes: The child first enters a 30-second cancellable suspension, so natural completion is impossible within the process bound. The parent records scope-exit before returning; exact output child-start,scope-exit,child-cancelled,after-scope proves both implicit cancellation and the scope-exit join.

nativeFact: An early return cancels an unconsumed async-let child and joins it before the caller receives the returned value.
notes: The child is already inside a 30-second cancellable suspension when the function records early-return. Exact output is child-start,early-return,child-cancelled,returned,after-return in 20 Swift 6.3.3 runs; the caller-side returned event therefore proves cleanup completed first.

nativeFact: Throwing out of a scope cancels and joins an unconsumed async-let child before the owner error reaches the caller's catch.
notes: The nonthrowing child catches cancellation inside a 30-second suspension, so it cannot replace the owner's error. Exact output is child-start,scope-throw,child-cancelled,caught,after-catch in 20 Swift 6.3.3 runs.

nativeFact: Lexical cleanups unwind in reverse registration order: when defer is registered before an async-let child, child cancellation and join complete before that defer executes.
notes: The child is already inside a 30-second cancellable suspension at scope exit. Exact output is child-start,scope-exit,child-cancelled,defer,after-scope in 20 Swift 6.3.3 runs, proving the relative cleanup order rather than a scheduler accident.

nativeFact: Lexical cleanups unwind in reverse registration order: when defer is registered after an async-let child, that defer executes before child cancellation and join.
notes: The child is already inside a 30-second cancellable suspension at scope exit. Exact output is child-start,scope-exit,defer,child-cancelled,after-scope in 20 Swift 6.3.3 runs, proving the reverse relative order without constraining unrelated scheduling.

nativeFact: Awaiting a throwing async-let binding waits for the child outcome and propagates its failure into the parent's do/catch.
notes: The child crosses an explicit yield before throwing the fixture's only error. Exact output is caught in 20 Swift 6.3.3 runs; no ready-task ordering is asserted.

nativeFact: Cancelling a parent suspended on an async-let value propagates cancellation to the structured child; the child's cancellation completes before the parent receives CancellationError, which the parent may catch and then return successfully.
notes: A MainActor flag is set immediately before the parent reaches the incomplete value wait, while the child is held in a cancellable 30-second suspension. Exact output is child-start,parent-await,child-cancelled,parent-caught,parent-finished in 20 Swift 6.3.3 runs.

nativeFact: withTaskGroup creates structured group children, and waitForAll does not return until every added child has completed.
notes: The child marks entry and waits behind an explicit gate. Exact output is child-start,parent-open,child-end,group-finished,after-scope in 20 Swift 6.3.3 runs; every edge is forced by the gate, waitForAll, or parent program order.

nativeFact: Returning normally from a withTaskGroup body implicitly waits for outstanding children without cancelling them before the outer scope continues.
notes: The child starts behind an explicit gate; the body records body-return and opens the gate immediately before returning without waitForAll. Exact output is child-start,body-return,child-end,after-scope in 20 Swift 6.3.3 runs, proving normal completion and the implicit join.

nativeFact: TaskGroup.cancelAll requests cancellation for outstanding children, while waitForAll and group scope exit still join each child before outer execution continues.
notes: The child has entered a 30-second cancellable suspension before cancel-all. Exact output is child-start,cancel-all,child-cancelled,child-finished,group-finished,after-scope in 20 Swift 6.3.3 runs, separating the cancellation request from completion and join.

diagnosticContains: expression is 'async' but is not marked with 'await'

notes: Compiler-backed preflight remains M7. M4 still rejects the direct runtime read instead of exposing its internal task carrier, and lexical cleanup cancels and joins the child.
